messages.subject: Harrow v Melbourne Sealtech - initial strategy
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah, Elena,

Having reviewed the supply agreement, two things jump out. Clause 8.1 gives us a clean express warranty (grade CG-218, two light bands flatness, 25,000 hour life). But clauses 11 and 12 are a problem - an indirect/consequential loss exclusion and a liability cap at the price paid for the seals (~£398k). The Pennland loss of profit (£985k) is squarely in the firing line.

Proposed approach: metallurgy first to nail breach, then push hard on the loss of profit being direct rather than consequential. Views?

Tom

Tom Gallagher
Associate, Dispute Resolution
Whitfield Carter LLP | 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
